articleTitle: Generating Captions for Images through Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In recent years, there has been rapid development in Artificial Intelligence (AI), with a particular focus on image captioning, which has garnered significant interest among scientists. This field involves automatically generating “natural language descriptions based on the objects identified within an image”, contributing to the broader context of scene understanding. This study conducts image caption generation using “deep learning techniques”. The study uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). “The image features are extracted from VGG16. The system is evaluated using two measures: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) and Metric for Evaluation of Translation with Explicit Ordering (METEOR). For BLEU-1, with 20 epochs, a value of 0.536 indicates that approximately 53.6% of the unigrams in the generated captions match those in the reference captions on average.

articleTitle: A Super Learner Ensemble-based Intrusion Detection System to Mitigate Network Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Governments and corporate institutions are now mostly reliant on integrated digital infrastructures. These digital infrastructures are usually targets of cyber threats such as intrusion, for which intrusion detection systems (IDS) have emerged. One of the key needs for a robust IDS includes reducing the rate of false positives and thus improving accuracy. In this study, three traditional machine learning (ML) algorithms, including K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), and Decision Tree (DT), and three ensemble Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBOOST), were used on the UNSW-NB15 dataset from the Australian Centre for Cyber Security’s Cyber Range Lab, to train intrusion detection models. A super-learner ensemble model was then built using the best two ensemble models (XGBOOST and RF) along with the best traditional model (KNN) as its base learners. The super-learner ensemble model was able to reduce false positives and improve detection accuracy with 98% accuracy. The model was then deployed in an IDS application to mitigate network attacks effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: Leveraging Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis to Improve Digital Bank Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Digital banking applications have experienced significant growth in the recent years. To create a positive perception towards the applications, customer reviews may be utilized to identify the possible improvements for the applications. In this research, firstly, the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model is applied to obtain the topics that are discussed in the reviews. Five topics are discovered in the case study, in which the number of topics is selected by the coherence score metric. A sentiment analysis using SenticNet 5 lexicon is subsequently performed, along with the part-of-speech tagging and dependency tree parsing for each sentence, to obtain the sentiment towards specific attributes of the application. The Opportunity Landscape Map visualizes the connection between the topics and the sentiment, such that the user experience topic is identified as underserved in the case study. The examples of potential improvements are adding features for account mutation, paying credit card bills, and changing phone number.

articleTitle: Integration of Stratified KFold Cross Validation to Enhance Prediction Accuracy: A Comparison Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Several researchers explore the impact of using KFold cross-validation in enhancing the model’s prediction performance. Improvement in the accuracy was shown in the available presented researches’ findings. The previous study focuses on feature selection methods and comparison of algorithms to declare the best-performing predictive model in forecasting students’ success to graduate from a real-world dataset in a 70/30 split. To further develop a better predictive model, this study integrated stratified KFold cross-validation to the same binary encoded dataset but an 80/20 split. The result shows that in NFS, 4/7 classifiers increased accuracy and L2 only 3/7. Meanwhile, in L1 feature selection, all seven (7/7) classifiers were seen to improve accuracy and decision Tree with a 14% increase compared to those not using stratified KFold cross-validation. On the other hand, only 3/7 in Genetic Algorithm (GA) with 5/7 improvement in AUC. However, there was a 28% decrease in accuracy using Naïve Bayes. The findings revealed that with the L1 selection method, seven classifiers performed better integrated with cross-validation than none. Moreover, GA and Random Forest earned the highest accuracy (0.79) and AUC (0.75), 4% higher than GA and Logistic without cross-validation.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Building System to Recognize Deaf Language Using BlazePalm and LSTM Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This paper is carried out to serve the learning and research process on the trends of modern technology and its application to real life. The paper addresses two problems. Firstly, the system will detect the hands in the frame and extract their features. Secondly, it recognizes the meaning of gestures from hand cues. We select the BlazePalm model, a highly renowned Google model for detecting human posture and gesture for the first problem. We then used a long short-term memory (LSTM) model to train with the key points extracted from the video using the above-mentioned model for the second problem. Besides, we have built a model for recognizing the sign language of the Vietnamese and combined it into sentences with an accuracy of 96.25% for 16 actions by combining the two models and input data being video actions. The simulation results show that the model can be applied to education and daily life.

articleTitle: Distributing Classical Information via Quantum Secret Sharing Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The possibility of distributing classical information between distinct users is discussed. Our technique based on transferring the e classical string is into two different quantum strings by using local operation. The obtained results show that both receivers could obtain the maximum information that encoded on the initial classical strings. However, in some case, one of them obtain the sent information completely, while the other received it partially. The obtained information depends on the initial quantum string which encodes the classical information. We expect that these results could be helpful on distributing quantum passwords and quantum key distribution

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Application to Facilitate Employee Voice in IT Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Cloud-based technology is becoming prevalent in offices as firms seek to increase productivity and improve accessibility. The key strategy to enhance employee engagement and organisational involvement is listening to employees. Employee voice refers to how employees communicate with their employers and influence workplace decisions. This paper investigates the implementation and potential advantages of a cloud-based feedback management system intended to promote and enhance employee voice in organisations. The study collected primary data by conducting semi-structured interviews with 48 employees from IT companies based in India. The authors selected 7–8 employees from different organisations with different perspectives on cloud-based applications. The authors have also introduced the cloud-based employee voice model for implementing and advancing the feedback process in organisations. This model will help organisations to increase employee engagement, satisfaction and overall organisational performance.

articleTitle: Certain Investigations on Classification of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a persistently progressing neurological disease with restricted treatment choices. The advent of extensive global datasets and advanced machine learning models offers new opportunities to evaluate potential prognostic, inspection, and diagnostic indicators. Additionally, emerging categorization and staging systems aim to accurately stratify patients into distinct prognostic categories. This study evaluates several prominent machine learning classifiers for ALS classification. These experiments have exposed that the CatBoost classification algorithm attained the maximum performance, with an accuracy of 0.85 and an AUC of 0.97. Other significant models include XGB, Random Forest, and Extra-Trees classifiers, each showing an accuracy of around 0.75 but with varying AUC values.

articleTitle: Load Shifting of Residential Load for Demand Side Management Using Tunicate Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Demand Side Management (DSM) is a critical strategy in the improvement of efficiency and reliability of the electrical system in smart grids. One of the effective DSM strategies is load shifting, which involves changing the timing of electricity consumption to off-peak hours. This paper gives a new approach to load shifting within residential areas through the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm. The TSA is an algorithm inspired by the swarming behavior of marine organisms called tunicates. These organisms are well known for their efficiency in movement and resource use. It is desired, within the scope of the proposed method, to optimize schedules for household appliances towards minimal electricity cost and minimal peak demand. TSA-based load-shifting technique: simulation result comparison with classical techniques—genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization. It should be stated that the simulation results show a comparison of the performance of this proposed TSA-based technique about cost reduction and the mitigation of peak demand, which outperformed both GA and PSO. The results obtained in this study demonstrated that the TSA-based technique offers much potential for effective residential load management in smart grids, where quantifiable benefits could be derived in terms of energy savings and system stability. In the future, work will focus on real-world implementation and integration with other DSM strategies to enhance the overall efficiency of the electrical grid. This research adds to the ever-increasing bank of bio-inspired algorithms for energy management and acts as a springboard toward further areas of investigation in the field.

articleTitle: The Trend of Published Research for Predicting Bankruptcy Via Machine Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Bibliometric analysis is a valuable technique for quantitative research on academic output to analyze pre-existing materials and address research patterns in a particular field. This paper aims to investigate machine learning approaches in predicting business failure. The findings suggest that author collaboration remains lacking despite a recent rise in publications, particularly internationally. Furthermore, We note that the subject of bankruptcy prediction has not placed enough emphasis on some machine-learning techniques. For example, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel at processing images rather than numbers. In addition to (CNN), Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks have also faced limitations in their application within this field due to several factors, including the requirement for large datasets and the necessity to investigate the “black box” of these models. These obstacles present opportunities for researchers to improve existing work in this area. This study has implications for theory and practice. In the first place, it gives academics knowledge about the intellectual framework and theoretical development of this topic, which is helpful for future research. Secondly, the study illuminates underutilized machine learning techniques for bankruptcy prediction, which hold significant value for corporate firm managers and policymakers regarding management and decision-making.

articleTitle: A Study on Advanced Techniques for Fractional Differential Equations: Integrating the Frobenius Method, ZZ Transform, and Diverse Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study explores fractional differential equations using fractional calculus techniques, extending the traditional Frobenius method with approaches like the ZZ transform and binomial series expansions. It presents efficient techniques for solving such equations and provides examples of their use in problem solving. Also, the study uses machine learning methodologies to solve approximate solutions; it also creates data sets for various fractional differential equations. The study assesses model accuracy by the plots of histograms, scatter plots, box plots, and learning curves. Accordingly, these findings provide an improved comprehension of the capacities of machine learning regarding the solution of such fractional differential equations.

Author Keywords: ZZ transform of the fractional derivative

articleTitle: Comparing Linear Regression, Random Forest and Support Vector Machine for Rental House Price Forecasting in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The real estate sector in Bahrain plays a pivotal role in its economy, with factors such as land price and house price predictions being crucial. Previous studies have addressed the importance of land price prediction in Bahrain [1]. In this study, data was collected from three famous real estate websites in Bahrain for a single day in March 2024. The dataset contains 14 attributes (such as property type, size, number of bedrooms, number of bathrooms, etc.) and 3084 instances, with 80% used for training and 20% for testing. “A comparative analysis of three data mining methods, namely Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine”, for rental house price forecasting in Bahrain was conducted. Unlike previous studies, this research focuses on rental house prices in Bahrain using a diverse set of attributes. “The performance of each model was evaluated using metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)”. Linear Regression (LR) had the highest MAE value of 0.1746, while SMOreg had a lower MAE of 0.1681. The lowest MAE was 0.1385, found with Random Forest (RF). The RMSE value for SMOreg was 0.2976, which was higher than LR’s 0.2935. In contrast, the lowest RMSE value was for RF with 0.2394. This paper found the Random Forest data mining method to perform the best.

articleTitle: Automated Emotion Recognition from Facial Expressions using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In the era of digital communication, it is more about being able to detect emotions than anything else if we are to maintain this complicated and demanding human society. Emotion recognition research is pulling out all the stops, resulting in all manner of methods to recognize human feelings. Emotions are often transmitted through words and body language, and facial expressions play an important part in communicating them. In this paper, the use of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed as a real-time emotion recognition system based on machine learning algorithm, and the system is able to process video feeds. The classifier breaks emotions down into seven categories, with an accuracy of about 81 percent. In addition, the research extends to the use of various image datasets to improve emotion forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: ESG Score Prediction Using Machine Learning, Gap Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study aims to identify the main research gaps in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) score prediction using Machine Learning (ML). To achieve this, a qualitative approach is adopted based on a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, alongside gap analysis employing the seven research gaps model developed by Miles. Considering the detailed gap analysis conducted above, several research problems can be derived from the identified practical knowledge, empirical, and population research gaps for further analysis and future studies: the lack of proper input features, the absence of novel ML models, the lack of diverse datasets testing, inadequate market diversity in testing, and a lack of recent years testing. This study not only contributes to the body of knowledge by finding the main gaps identified in recent studies but also has the potential to inspire researchers to address these gaps and potentially revolutionize the field, thereby fostering innovation and advancement in ESG score prediction using ML. By addressing these gaps, researchers can significantly enhance the accuracy and reliability of ESG score prediction models, leading to more informed decision-making in the field.

articleTitle: Clustering Rental Houses in Bahrain Using K Modes Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Clustering is a key application in big data, essential for unsupervised learning. This study tackles the challenge of clustering a dataset with categorical housing attributes in Bahrain to uncover meaningful patterns and insights. Using the K-Modes algorithm, tailored for categorical data, the analysis includes features such as property type, location, number of bedrooms, and amenities. The performance is evaluated using the Silhouette score, which was 0.208, indicating moderate clustering effectiveness. The findings highlight distinct categories of residential properties in Bahrain, with Governorate being the feature with the highest differences among clusters. This research provides valuable insights into the Bahraini real estate market, aiding stakeholders in property development, urban planning, and housing policy formulation to make informed decisions and address market needs.

articleTitle: PMAssist: Scaling Product Efficiency using GenAI
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Software Product Management (SPM) is a broad discipline that spans technology and business domains, requiring extensive collaboration between development teams and client stakeholders. Product managers are integral throughout the product lifecycle, from ideation to product launch and development to ongoing monitoring and maintenance. Product managers frequently encounter challenging situations that impair their ability to make effective decisions in a data-driven environment. In this paper, we present PMAssist, a product management tool developed using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to enhance product management efficiency. PMAssist offers an innovative AI-driven solution to the tedious tasks of document retrieval and report generation. This research provides a GenAI-based tool that product managers can leverage to solve complex, time-consuming, and labor-intensive manual processes involved in product management. Instead, they can focus more on strategic and tactical tasks.

articleTitle: Strengthening Cryptographic Protocols: Leveraging the Soham Transform’s Unique Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This article presents a new cryptographic technique combining Soham transformation technique with congruence modulo operator for improving the security of data. The method utilises mathematical formulas to code and decode the messages to and from the receiver in an encrypted manner so as to enhance security. The work assesses the computational complexity, the robustness against attacks, and the possibility of scaling up the procedure and discusses the usefulness of the approach. Experimental research supports the method in achieving the objectives of protecting data through different channels of communications. This innovative technique in computational mathematics has a potential to lead in the development of complex cryptographical systems that are needed in the current traditional and emerging digital business world where security is paramount.

articleTitle: Enhancing Q-Learning with Vector Similarity and Tabu Search for Solving the Vehicle Routing Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In recent years, addressing the m-Dial-a-Ride variant of the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) has become an important research area. This paper presents a novel model that aims to effectively represent this variant by leveraging a combination of well-known techniques and original approaches. The model incorporates Q-learning, embedding vector-based knowledge representation and interpolation, and tabu search to improve the bus shuttle routing problem and reduce waiting times. The implementation of this model yielded satisfactory results, with a significant 27% reduction in the 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentile waiting times for passengers. By comparing it to the optimal solution calculated using brute force in a previous paper for the same real-life dataset, the trained model’s predictions deviate on average by approximately 20% from the optimal. Considering the model was trained with a limited number of iterations and demonstrated the ability to transfer knowledge to new inputs without over-fitting, this performance is commendable. The model effectively captures the dynamics between demand and its impact on waiting times. While the model shows promise, the paper concludes with the limitations and further work that need to be addressed in future research.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Identification of Pesticide Residue
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Pesticides are chemical substances that are regularly used by farmers to enhance crop yields through controlling pests that harm plants. However, despite the crucial role that pesticides play in agriculture, they pose potential risks to the environment and may have chronic effects on human health and hence raise key concerns about food safety. Therefore, adopting food control systems to identify pesticide residue in food is of major importance. This study explored the capabilities of various machine learning models to detect pesticide residue in food samples. To this end, the study considered data collected from Bahrain’s Pesticide Residue Monitoring Program spanning the period 2015–2019. For comparison purposes, different classification methods have been implemented covering K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Quadratic Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayes, and Support Vector Machine. The conducted analysis revealed that machine learning models can effectively detect pesticide residue with an overall accuracy of 75%. However, the performance of the adopted models can be improved by different directions such as introducing relevant variables, addressing imbalanced data issues, and considering advanced deep learning models.

articleTitle: Initial State Time-Dependent Quantum Game
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The possibility of implementing a time dependent version of Eisert, Wilkens, and Lewenstein (EWL), quantum game is discussed. It is assumed that the players initial states are time dependent, while the entangling quantum gate either time dependent or independent during the game. The obtained results shows that the players payoff depend on their initial state, while The time-independent entangling gate has a minor impact on the game compared to its time-dependent counterpart. However, one can improve the lower bounds of the payoffs by using time dependent gate. Moreover, the exponential form of the entangling power is more powerful than the linear one, where the payoffs are much better. However, the maximum potential rewards in this game may be lower than those attainable in the classical game, the minimum guaranteed outcomes are much better.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Ant Colony Optimization for Parkinson’s Disease Classification Based on Synthetic Minority Oversampling and Adaptive Synthetic Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurological ailment of the nervous system, first characterized in 1817. Around 90% of PD patients experience speech problems. Therefore, early detection and identification of PD are critical for disease progression and treatment. This study proposes a unique approach for detecting PD using features extracted from speech signals of patients with PD. We categorize the hybrid machine learning (ML) technique into two stages: (i) pre-processing of data, followed by (ii) hybrid ant colony optimization (ACO), and (iii) classification using the extra tree, cat boost, and Xgboost. However, the PD data set’s class distribution is skewed (unbalanced). Therefore, we applied the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Adaptive Synthetic technique (ADASYN) to balance this unbalanced data. We classified the PD dataset using the hybrid ACO with extra tree, hybrid ACO with cat boost, and hybrid ACO with Xgboost classification methods after transforming it to a balanced majority class. The suggested hybrid methods, which combine SMOTE-ACO+extra tree, and ADASYN-ACO+Extra tree gave classification accuracy rates of 99.28%, and 95.72%. The results indicated that the proposed hybrid ACO technique produced promising results in PD classification.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graphs-Based Halal Food Provider Information Search System at Surabaya
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In Indonesia, approximately 10% of products possess halal certification. Consequently, there is a need for a solution, specifically a system capable of retrieving information from halal food providers and generating recommendations. We crawl the BPJPH API. Subsequently, the ranking of food providers is determined using the Node Similarity algorithm and graph embedding utilizing the Node2vec and Fast Random Projection algorithms in conjunction with the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm. A simple search engine application was then developed using StreamLit, an open-source Python-based application framework designed to facilitate the creation of web applications in the fields of machine learning and data science. Application development also incorporates SQLiteStudio for database creation. Following the search engine application design process, an evaluation stage was conducted using two metrics: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), a metric to assess each process that gives potential answers to a query arranged in order of their likelihood of being correct, and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), a metric that evaluates performance of a ranking list by penalizing incorrect sequence in the list. Overall, the performances of systems that use Node Similarity and K-Nearest Neighbors with Fast Random Projection algorithms are generally better than the performance of system that uses K-Nearest Neighbors with Node2Vec Algorithms.

articleTitle: Small and Medium Enterprises’ Digital Transformation Intention based on the Trade-off Theory: Role of Perceived Benefit and Perceived Privacy Disclosure Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are critical for economic growth but often lag in digital transformation. Adoption decisions depend on the trade-off between expected benefits and perceived risks. This study develops and tests a research model grounded in trade-off theory to explain SMEs’ digital transformation intentions based on perceived benefits and perceived privacy disclosure risks. A survey was conducted with 212 SME leaders in Vietnam. The results of structural equation modeling support hypotheses that perceived benefits positively influence perceived value and digital transformation intention, while perceived privacy disclosure risk negatively impacts perceived value and intention. Perceived value positively affects intention, supporting its role as the cognitive trade-off mechanism. The findings validate applying trade-off theory to examine how SMEs weigh expected benefits and perceived risks in forming digital transformation intentions. Theoretical contributions include enriching technology adoption research and empirically examining the undertheorized risk of privacy disclosure. Practical implications suggest emphasizing communicating benefits, addressing privacy concerns, and reshaping the benefit-risk trade-off calculus to promote digital adoption among SMEs.

articleTitle: HEterogenous RAnking CummuLativE System - HERACLES
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Optimal portfolio selection can be supported by the new trends in Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning, and Portfolio Theory, examined in 4 neural system groups. The novel HEterogenous RAnking CumuLativE System – HERACLES, implements the optimal classifier that is discovered on the portfolio selection, to address key aspects of literature and the markets such as, the: i) Fractal Market Hypothesis (FMH) patterns in the Entropy of returns affected by the Chaotic Dynamics and following Kappa Distributions, ii) behavioral performance of investors, iii) detection of an optimal classifier on 1 Voted Perceptron (VP), 46 Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs), 66 Modulars (MDNs), 60 Self-Organized Feature Maps models (SOFMs), in Neuro or/and Hybrid Neural-Genetic systems to optimise investments. HERACLES acts as a dragon-slayer to prevent bubbles in the markets.

articleTitle: Stroke Detection and Diagnosis in CT Scan Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This research introduces a system capable of automatically distinguishing between normal and stroke-affected CT scans. The model developed aims to significantly reduce the workload on radiologists by providing an efficient tool for reading and analyzing CT scans. Hence, the human error could be minimized. To develop the Deep learning-based Stroke Detection and Diagnosis (DSDD), a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) model was employed due to its superior performance and high accuracy in medical image classification tasks. The dataset used in this research, sourced from Kaggle, comprises both normal and abnormal (stroke) CT scan images. The results of the classification demonstrate that the DSDD is highly effective, correctly classifying the majority of images within the dataset. The system achieves impressive metrics, including high accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and an elevated F1-Score. These outcomes indicate that the DSDD is a reliable and valuable tool for the automatic detection and diagnosis of strokes in CT scan images.

articleTitle: Towards a New Hybrid Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique for Imbalanced Problem in Software Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The software industry strives to improve software quality through continuous bug prediction, bug elimination, and module fault prediction. This issue has piqued researchers’ interest because of its significant relevance in the software industry. Frequently, Software Defect Prediction (SDP) models contain significantly skewed data, making it difficult for classifiers to recognize defective occurrences. The machine learning (ML) community has put a lot of effort into solving the problem of learning from imbalanced SDP data, though less so in empirical software engineering. The over-sampling strategy is one of many recent solutions to this problem. This strategy balances the number of defective and non-defective cases by creating new defective instances. Unfortunately, these methods would result in non-diverse synthetic instances as well as a large number of unneeded noise instances, creating an imbalanced class problem. As a result, we propose a hybrid synthetic minority oversampling (HSMOTE) to address the problem of imbalance in SDP. In this paper, we introduce the hybrid Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (HSMOTE), a method that utilizes Extra Tree, Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (Xgboost) for classification. We develop and deploy the proposed method on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) dataset, evaluating its performance on three datasets: JM1, KC1, and PC3. We compared the parameters for accuracy, precision, AUC, recall, F-measure, and Mathew Correlation Coefficient to those of the existing SDP. The findings from the simulations on the JM1 data showed that the proposed techniques work better than the current best models. The proposed SMOTE+RF technique surpasses the existing techniques with an accuracy of 93.69%, an AUC of 82.70%, and an F-measure of 32.98%. Similarly, the proposed SMOTE+Xgboost method outperforms the existing techniques with an accuracy of 93.432%, an AUC of 82.64%, and an F-measure of 34.13%, while SMOTE+ET achieved an accuracy of 93.43%, an AUC of 77.68%, and an F-measure of 31.90%.

articleTitle: Generating MRI Images Based on Clinical Text Using Diffusion Models for Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The synthesis of realistic images from textual descriptions has advanced significantly, particularly through the adoption of diffusion models. These models use probabilistic techniques and iterative refinement to produce high-fidelity visual representations. This research investigates the use of diffusion models in the field of medical imaging, with a particular emphasis on generating MRI scans for breast cancer patients using textual descriptions of their medical conditions. We utilize a text-to-image stable diffusion model and a text-to-video diffusion model to create synthetic MRI images and sequences, respectively. The Duke Breast Cancer MRI dataset, which includes diverse imaging modalities and patient metadata, is used for this purpose. Performance is evaluated using metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Kernel Inception Distance (KID) for images, and Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) and CLIP similarity scores for videos. Our experiments reveal that text-to-image synthesis with diffusion models can effectively generate high-quality MRI images, with performance influenced by the choice of text tokenization methods, as indicated by a KID metric score of 0.97 for text-to-image models using the CLIP tokenizer. Text-to-video models show potential, with a CLIP similarity metric score of 25.38. These advancements suggest new opportunities for enhancing diagnostic interpretation and augmenting datasets.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Detecting Financial Statement Fraud: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of publishing, citation, and collaboration trends in financial statement fraud detection using Machine Learning (ML) from 2010 to 2023. By utilizing data from Scopus and Google Scholar, the analysis was conducted in R Studio, identifying key thematic and collaborative patterns across ML, artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, and predictive modeling. The results highlight significant advancements in fraud detection, driven largely by international collaborations between countries such as China-Australia, Canada-UAE, and Belgium-Netherlands. Notably, fraud-related research has begun to surpass ML and AI in keyword trends, indicating a shift in focus within the field. Node analysis further exposes key topics within collaborative networks, emphasizing the growing relevance of machine learning in fraud detection. These findings offer critical insights for researchers, policymakers, and industry professionals, providing a clearer understanding of the evolving global research landscape and its implications for the future of fraud detection technologies.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Trajectory Optimization Methods for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The optimization of the trajectory of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial to maximize operational efficiency and resource conservation. five trajectory optimization approaches for UAVs: the Dinkelbach Algorithm, Mixed-Integer Non-Convex Optimization, Newton’s Method, Genetic Algorithm, and Conjugate Gradient Method. Non-convex methods offer algorithmic flexibility, while the Dinkelbach Algorithm is renowned for its robustness and ability to solve mixed-integer optimization problems. Using detailed simulations, we evaluate the performance of these five approaches in terms of computation time, precision of the optimal trajectory, and resilience to environmental disturbances. Our results reveal distinct advantages for each method, thus providing valuable insights for the development of efficient trajectory planning systems tailored to the specific needs of UAV missions in diverse and dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Virtual Clothes Fitting: Leveraging Computer Vision and Deep Learning for a Seamless Online Shopping Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The digital transformation of the fashion industry has led to the surge of online shopping, but the absence of a virtual fitting room remains a significant challenge. Without the ability to try on clothes virtually, online shoppers may hesitate to make purchases due to concerns about fit, leading to higher return rates. To address this issue, researchers have proposed a virtual clothes fitting system that utilizes computer vision and deep learning. By employing the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) developed in this research, consumers can virtually try on clothing, even those that are not physically available. The model’s effectiveness was evaluated through user feedback, and the proposed system emphasizes inclusivity by offering a wide range of clothing sizes and styles to cater to diverse body types and encourage a more inclusive online shopping experience.

articleTitle: Evaluating Automatic Transcription Models Utilising Cloud Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology is becoming pervasive in society and is being used for language translation, customer service and disability support. ASR and transcription is also rapidly becoming a popular manner of enabling qualitative research. Traditionally transcribing interviews and focus groups would have been very time consuming and labour intensive. In recent years, online tools have become available to help with automatic transcription. These tools have varying levels of accuracy, and most will require manual correction. Moreover, these tools require a researcher to manually upload audio files that have been processed or edited.This research proposes the development of an automatic framework for completing ASR and automatic transcription without the need for the researcher to perform any manual processes. The research is completed within an industrial context in an organisation that completes qualitative analysis and evaluation on behalf of clients in the third sector. The proposed framework utilises a cloud-based API for completing the automatic transcription. This research evaluates multiple APIs for completing automatic transcription and selects one service for inclusion within the framework. This evaluation is completed on a self-created audio dataset named “S3QualitativeAudio” using Word Error Rate (WER) calculation on the transcription and also based on cost-benefit analysis. The research has determined that the Whisper ASR model developed by OpenAI provides the lowest error rate of those evaluated (most accurate with 96% of the audio files providing the lowest WER value). The average WER for the Whisper ASR model was 0.07246. Further evaluation was completed using this model in an attempt to decrease the error rate further. The final automatic transcriptions could be used for sentiment analysis and text summarisation to complete further qualitative analysis.

articleTitle: Crosschecking Verification Over the Ethereum Blockchain Using QR Scannable Products
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Counterfeit products pose a significant threat to global economies, undermining consumer trust and damaging brand reputations. Traditional verification methods often prove ineffective in combating the proliferation of counterfeit goods. This research explores the integration of QR codes and Ethereum blockchain technology to enhance product verification within supply chains, offering a more secure and transparent solution. The proposed research aims to foster trust, transparency, and consumer confidence by generating unique QR codes linked to digital counterparts on the blockchain. The system enables dynamic interactions between consumers and the authentication process through a user-friendly mobile interface, where QR codes serve as secure anchors for product information verified against blockchain entries. The research encompasses the development of smart contracts, a user-friendly interface, and comprehensive testing to ensure the system’s scalability and reliability. Overall, this research demonstrates the potential of combining QR codes and blockchain technology to revolutionise product verification within supply chains, providing a more secure, efficient, and reliable means of combating counterfeiting.

articleTitle: Developing a Strategic Framework for Cloud Adoption in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Education is a cornerstone of economic growth and development, especially in emerging nations. Its role has expanded significantly with the integration of information technology. The requirement for educational institutions to have information technology infrastructure, in addition to the ongoing upkeep of such infrastructure, is a significant strain on those institutions, particularly during times of economic turmoil. Computing in the cloud consequently becomes a favoured alternative for maintaining an optimal level of service quality despite the limited resources that are currently accessible in organizations. Cloud computing, which is a constantly changing idea, has been a cause of innovations and improvements in Information Technology and more importantly in education. The virtualization of resources in addition to this technology’s flexibility and scalability justifies its ongoing acceptance at a wide variety of educational institutions. This research discusses cloud computing technology given its applications in education, and most significantly, a comprehensive overview of earlier work in this field.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition: Fight Detection using Long term Recurrent Convolutional Network (LRCN)
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition for Fight Detection is an important research domain aimed at automatically identifying patterns indicative of physical altercations. Leveraging deep learning models like CNNs and RNNs, this approach extracts features from video frames to recognize fight-related behavioural patterns. The primary objective is to develop a machine learning model capable of autonomously detecting instances of fights in video footage, using techniques such as the Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Network (LRCN). Training involves a comprehensive dataset encompassing examples of both fights and non-fight activities, with model performance evaluated using standard metrics. Each frame undergoes individual analysis by the model to predict the presence of any indications of a fight. The model predicts the action with an accuracy of 98.03% and the movements given as input can be categorized as fights or no fights.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Open Generative Artificial Intelligence into Software Supply Chain Security
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: While new technologies emerge, human errors always looming. Software supply chain is increasingly complex and intertwined, the security of a service has become paramount to ensuring the integrity of products, safeguarding data privacy, and maintaining operational continuity. In this work, we conducted experiments on the promising open Large Language Models (LLMs) into two main software security challenges: source code language errors and deprecated code, with a focus on their potential to replace conventional static and dynamic security scanners that rely on predefined rules and patterns. Our findings suggest that while LLMs present some unexpected results, they also encounter significant limitations, particularly in memory complexity and the management of new and unfamiliar data patterns. Despite these challenges, the proactive application of LLMs, coupled with extensive security databases and continuous updates, holds the potential to fortify Software Supply Chain (SSC) processes against emerging threats.

articleTitle: Predicting Environmental, Social, and Governance Scores with Machine Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The paramount factors in assessing sustainability and the social responsibility of business are environmental, social, and governance (ESG). Over the last few years, leveraging machine learning (ML) methods in predicting ESG scores has preserved significant recognition due to its possibility of enhancing prediction accuracy, investment practices, and decision-making processes by stakeholders, policymakers, and investors. Our research uses ML methods to synthesize recent findings from scholarly articles on ESG score prediction. The systematic literature review (SLR) elucidates diverse areas of previous literature, such as datasets, methodology, metrics, and findings. The finding of SLR illustrates the significant application of ML to predict ESG scores, especially by Random Forest. The research paves the way for practical implications for stakeholders seeking long-term investment practices. However, it also underscores the pressing need for further studies to explore the capabilities of other ML models and enhance their capabilities through integrating hybrid models or feature engineering, thereby ensuring the continued improvement and relevance of ESG score prediction.

articleTitle: Stock Portfolio Optimization Using Metaheuristic and Deep Learning Algorithms: Evidence from Boursa Kuwait
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: There has been considerable interest in portfolio optimization, also known as POP, in the literature, which has led to the development of various theories and methodologies designed to enhance its accuracy and alignment with real-world conditions. This research delves into the resolution of POP by leveraging higher moments derived from expected return distributions, with the objective of precisely pinpointing a portfolio that generates positive returns while maintaining a lower risk profile favored by investors. The proposed model addresses this challenge by incorporating four key objectives: expected returns, skewness, conditional value at risk and kurtosis. Through converting the optimization problem into a non-linear programming system, the study leverages the daily stock prices of all stocks listed on Boursa Kuwait from January 2010 to December 2023 to identify the top 10 performing stocks through the utilization of the k-means clustering algorithm. Subsequently, the model employs long short-term memory to forecast the returns of the selected stocks and estimate their moments, which are then utilized by the genetic-algorithm and particle-swarm hybrid technique to determine the best investment allocations. Moreover, the algorithm integrates an automatic hyperparameter optimizer to fine-tune its settings and enhance performance. A comparative analysis with three other popular models validates the performance superiority of the study’s model using expected portfolio returns, risk levels, and risk-adjusted return ratios.

articleTitle: Skill Factor as a Key Indicator of Digital Dexterity in Emerging Countries: Cluster Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Cluster analysis is a data mining method that organizes similar objects based on their attributes. It is an unsupervised and quantitative form of classification that works on unlabeled data. One functional way to earn resilience and sustainability is through digital transformation which depends on digital skills. Therefore, in this article, the cluster analysis is used to segment 39 emerging countries based on their skills factor, which is a key indicator of digital skill in fourth industrial revaluation (4IR) era. We have chosen cluster analysis because it has several advantages, such as identifying homogeneous groups of countries in terms of skills factor, facilitating the study of digital dexterity in complex system that include several dimensions, showing readiness of countries to the adoption of 4IR and enhancing cooperation opportunities among countries. We do not aim to explore the connection between skills factor and digital variable. We only focus on using skill factor as a key indicator of digital skills in emerging countries by clustering the countries into four groups according to their skills. This can assist the decision-makers to evaluate, improve and compare the digital skills, training policies and strategies with other countries.
